minutes.headline: Green committee will pursue a townwide Mass Save building-assessment study before its next grant push
minutes.summary: The chair recapped a Mass Save Summit he attended, walking the task force through weatherization, heat-pump, building-management and electric-lawn-equipment incentive programs, plus new "portfolio prioritization" and building-assessment studies meant to get town buildings grant-ready. The group agreed to schedule a meeting with National Grid/Mass Save and the facilities director to start the portfolio study, put the Turkey Hill project on hold until then, reviewed the town's Green Community history and open incentive programs, and closed with brief updates on a styrofoam-recycling grant, school HVAC work, committee term expirations, and a motion on prior minutes.

budget_items.topic: FY25 Mass Save municipal energy efficiency accomplishments
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair cited statewide counts of municipal buildings converted to heat pumps, moved off oil/propane or gas, and weatherized under Mass Save's FY25 program.
Mass Save's prescriptive weatherization tier was described as raised for small buildings, with a custom-express tier covering most town buildings.
An incentive rate for air-sealing labor was cited from the summit materials as very generous.
Projects over 20,000 square feet must meet a minimum benefit-to-cost threshold to qualify for incentives.
Air-source and variable refrigerant flow heat pump rebates were quoted per ton of capacity.
Incentives for building management system upgrades were described as paid per square foot per control sequence, up to a capped number of sequences.
figures_as_heard: five or 10 cents per square foot

budget_items.what_was_said: Incentives for variable frequency/speed drive upgrades were described as covering a large share of project cost.
figures_as_heard: up to 50% of the project cost

budget_items.what_was_said: Rebates for battery-powered mowers, trimmers and leaf blowers were compared to gas equipment costs, including a larger town-scale zero-turn mower rebate.

budget_items.topic: Electric vehicle incentive vs fuel-efficient requirement
budget_items.what_was_said: A state incentive for switching to electric vehicles was described as too small relative to the added cost, under the Climate Leader vehicle-first requirement.

budget_items.topic: Prevailing wage effect on grant-funded work
budget_items.what_was_said: A member described a prior project where invoking the green grant triggered prevailing wage rules, sharply increasing the contractor quote; hourly wage comparisons were also cited.
figures_as_heard: the price went up three times

budget_items.what_was_said: New Climate Leader Communities grant tiers were described: technical support funding and a larger decarbonization accelerator grant covering a share of project cost.
figures_as_heard: 10% of a project cost up to a million dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: A new grant would cover most of the cost of battery-powered ride-on and stand-up mowers for municipalities.
figures_as_heard: up to 75% of the total cost

budget_items.what_was_said: A large multi-state federal award aimed at expanding heat pump adoption was mentioned as a major current funding push.
The town's original Green Communities designation grant was described as a one-time award used for early energy efficiency upgrades.
Subsequent Green Communities funding moved to a competitive round with a per-grant cap, most recently used for the primary school mini-splits.

budget_items.topic: Prior primary school mini-split project cost
budget_items.what_was_said: An earlier mini-split installation at the primary school, done without the green committee's early involvement, was described as costing far more than necessary for a limited number of units.

decisions.decision: Chair will take an action item to schedule a meeting with the facilities director and National Grid/Mass Save contacts to begin the portfolio prioritization plan (PPP) process, targeting early August.
The Turkey Hill project will be set aside until the portfolio prioritization plan (PPP) is completed first.
The committee's main push for August will be developing a townwide energy plan.
John Arno will fill out the town's talent bank form to be considered for appointment to the committee.

what_happened.line: The task force will seek a townwide building-assessment study through Mass Save before pursuing further building grants.
The Turkey Hill project is on hold until that assessment study is complete.
The group's main focus for August will be developing a townwide energy plan.
A resident said he will apply through the town's talent bank for appointment to the committee.

why_it_matters: The assessment study would shape which town buildings become eligible for state weatherization, heat-pump and building-management incentives, which can affect future capital budgets.
Pausing the Turkey Hill project ties its timeline to when the broader study is finished, so residents watching that project should expect delay.

A member described a past case where triggering a green grant required prevailing wage rules that raised a contractor's quote sharply -- a cost tradeoff worth watching as the town pursues more grant-funded building work.
watch_next: A meeting with the facilities director and National Grid/Mass Save, targeted for early August, to begin the portfolio prioritization plan.
Progress on the townwide energy plan the committee plans to develop in August.
